What happens on Days 1–5 of Visit 1 (CBCT, extractions, placement, temporary bridge)?

Visit 1 usually spans five working days: Day 1 covers 3D CBCT scans and treatment confirmation, Day 2 involves extractions and titanium or zirconia implant placement, Days 3–4 allow swelling control and lab fabrication of temporary teeth, and Day 5 completes your temporary bridge fitting and stitch check before flying home.

As outlined by [Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/dental-implant-surgery/about/pac-20384622), dental implant surgery happens in stages—starting with damaged tooth removal, bone preparation when needed, and surgical placement of the metal post. If your scan reveals insufficient jawbone density and your dentist recommends a sinus lift or bone graft, your team may adjust the Day 2 surgical time and lengthen the healing gap before Visit 2.

body.text: What healing happens during the 3–6 month osseointegration gap?

During the 3–6 month gap between visits, your jawbone grows tightly around the surface of each implant post in a biological process called osseointegration. This fusion creates a stable root capable of supporting permanent chewing forces without loosening, which is why rushing Visit 2 carries high mechanical risk.

Clinical guidance from [Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/dental-implant-surgery/about/pac-20384622) confirms that full bone growth and healing around dental implants takes several months. Lower jaw implants often integrate closer to three months because mandibular bone is denser, while upper jaw implants or grafted sites frequently need four to six months. Your dentist confirms readiness using an X-ray or stability test before clearing you to book Visit 2.
What happens on Days 1–7 of Visit 2 (impressions, trials, final bite)?

Visit 2 lasts six to seven days because permanent crowns or bridges require iterative lab work rather than surgery. Days 1–2 capture digital or physical impressions, Days 3–5 test framework fit, tooth shade, and speech in your mouth, and Days 6–7 finalize permanent fixation and bite balance.

Do not compress Visit 2 into a three-day weekend. Leaving two full days between the aesthetic try-in and final fitting gives the dental laboratory time to refine contact points, gum contours, and jaw alignment. If you notice a high spot when biting down on Day 6, a Day 7 morning buffer lets your dentist polish the occlusion before you head to the airport.
How do you coordinate flights for both visits?

Coordinate flights by booking Visit 1 as a standalone round-trip ticket with a 24-hour buffer after Day 5, and waiting to book Visit 2 until your dentist confirms your osseointegration timeframe. Flexible fare classes prevent costly rebooking fees if bone grafting extends healing or lab work needs an extra afternoon.

Before confirming any clinic, verify its International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate through the [Turkish Ministry of Health Health Tourism Department](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html) and review the pre-travel guidance published by the [U.S. Embassy in Türkiye](https://tr.usembassy.gov/medical-tourism/). faq.q: Can dental implants in Türkiye ever be finished in a single visit?
faq.a: True permanent crowns on freshly placed implants are rarely recommended in one trip because bone needs months to fuse. Some clinics place fixed temporary bridges during Visit 1, while final prosthetics still require Visit 2.

faq.q: Why does Visit 2 take longer than Visit 1?
faq.a: Visit 1 focuses on one surgical session plus brief monitoring, whereas Visit 2 depends on multiple laboratory stages—impressions, framework trials, porcelain layering, glazing, and bite checks—spaced across a full working week.

faq.q: What if a temporary crown comes loose during the 3–6 month gap at home?
faq.a: Temporary bridges are designed to be removable and lighter than final prosthetics. Ask your licensed dental team before leaving Visit 1 for written instructions on what a local dentist can safely re-cement if needed.

faq.q: Are soft foods required during both Visit 1 and Visit 2?
faq.a: Soft, lukewarm foods are essential during Visit 1 and the early healing weeks to protect sutures and freshly placed implants. During Visit 2, there is usually no major surgical swelling, so eating is much more comfortable once finals are fitted.

faq.q: Which airport is better for dental clinics in Istanbul?
faq.a: Istanbul Airport (IST) serves most European-side clinics, while Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) is closer to Anatolian-side districts. Choosing the closer airport can cut post-appointment transfer time by an hour in heavy traffic.
